Tesla Refutes FSD Shutdown Rumors in China

Reports emerged of Tesla winding down its Full Self-Driving (FSD) efforts in China. However, Tesla denied the reports, claiming they were “false” and confirmed that it was not shutting down its data center in Shanghai. Instead, Tesla is ramping up hiring for self-driving-related positions.

children: Musk Teases New Tesla Vehicle

Musk fueled speculation about a family-oriented vehicle possibly entering the Tesla lineup after a user urged the billionaire to make a minivan. Musk hinted at a new high-capacity vehicle, stating it would be “way cooler than a minivan.” Notably, Tesla has already unveiled the Robovan concept in the past.
Musk Talks Galaxy-Wide Expansion with Optimus Robots and Solar Power
The
Space Exploration Technologies Corp.

(NASDAQ:SPCX) CEO also discussed the potential of Tesla’s Optimus becoming the first-ever “Von Neumann” machine as SpaceX revealed plans for a new Starbase spaceport in Louisiana. The spaceport, estimated to cost over $100 billion, is expected to be self-sustaining and create 3,000 jobs. Read the full article here.
Tesla’s Largest Recall in China

Tesla is recalling nearly 3 million vehicles in China due to issues with the emergency door releases. This marks the company’s largest recall in the country. The recall was initiated after at least 15 deaths were reported in 12 crashes in which occupants or rescuers could not open the doors of burning Teslas. Read the full article here.
Tesla Increases Cybertruck Prices Amid Slow Sales
Despite sluggish sales, Tesla has raised the prices of its Cybertruck all-electric pickup truck in the U.S. by up to $5,000 for some trim levels. Read the full article here.
